01-1.caption: Guaman Poma's drawing (about 1615) of an Inca chasqui messenger blowing a conch-shell trumpet.

01-2.caption: An hourglass-shaped West African talking drum, with leather cords that tighten the drumhead to change its pitch.

01-3.author: danmairen
01-3.caption: The worn rammed-earth remains of a Great Wall beacon tower standing on a hill in northern China.

02-1.caption: A restored Chappe optical telegraph tower near Saverne, France, with its signal arms on a mast on top.

02-2.author: Staff photographer
02-2.caption: A modern museum reproduction of Volta's 1800 pile: a column of metal discs, the first electric battery.

02-3.author: Unknown authorUnknown author
02-3.caption: Michael Faraday's iron ring wrapped in wire coils, which he used to discover electromagnetic induction in 1831.

03-1.author: chailey
03-1.caption: Cooke and Wheatstone's 1837 five-needle telegraph at the Science Museum, London; the needles pointed to letters on the diamond board.

03-2.author: Zubro
03-2.caption: An early Morse telegraph register in a museum, which marked dots and dashes onto a long paper tape.

03-3.author: Unknown authorUnknown author or not provided
03-3.caption: Pony Express rider Frank E. Webner on horseback, around 1861, the year the telegraph line put the Pony Express out of business.

04-1.author: Robert Charles Dudley
04-1.caption: Robert Dudley's 1866 painting of the cable-laying machinery on the deck of the giant steamship Great Eastern.

04-2.author: Daderot
04-2.caption: A short piece of the first transatlantic telegraph cable of 1858, showing its twisted outer wires, in the Bennington Museum.

04-3.caption: William Thomson's 1858 mirror galvanometer, which detected the tiny signals arriving through the Atlantic cable.

05-1.author: Travok32

05-2.caption: A photograph of Antonio Meucci (1808-1889), the Italian-American inventor who worked on an early telephone.

05-3.caption: An engraved portrait of Elisha Gray, the American inventor who raced Alexander Graham Bell to patent the telephone.
